# Acnologia: full reference

> Acnologia is a self-hosted API key pool. It stores many API keys per provider, hands out a working key, detects rate limits and quota exhaustion, cools keys down and rotates. Consume it through the proxy (the key is injected and never exposed) or by leasing a key and reporting the outcome.

Contents: authentication, public endpoints, the consumer API (services, lease, report, renew, proxy), outcomes, concurrency, MCP, SDKs and other languages, resilience, cache and idempotency, service groups, app limits, egress proxies, webhooks, key secrecy and redaction, errors, admin tokens and the `acn` CLI, docs.

Conventions: JSON bodies; IDs are integers except `lease_id` (string); timestamps are RFC 3339 strings or null. Errors are `{"error": {"code": "string", "message": "string"}}` with a matching HTTP status.

## Authentication

Every consumer and MCP call carries an app token (`acn_...`) created on the dashboard Apps page. The token is shown once and stored only as a hash. An app can have several named tokens (for example one per deployment), each revocable on its own and optionally expiring; requests, spend and limits are counted per app, whichever token made the call. Tokens from before the rename (`cog_...`) keep working.

```
Authorization: Bearer acn_xxx
X-Acnologia-Token: acn_xxx            (alternative)
?acn_token=acn_xxx                    (proxy only, for URL-only tools)
```

Acnologia strips all of them before forwarding to the provider. An app can be restricted to some services (empty list means all) and to mode `proxy`, `lease` or `both`. A token that is missing, wrong, revoked or expired gets 401 (`app token revoked`, `app token expired`); a paused app gets 403; a service or mode the app may not use gets 403.

## Public endpoints

```
GET /healthz             -> 200 {"ok": true, "version": "1.0.0"}
GET /llms.txt            -> the short summary with links
GET /llms-full.txt       -> this reference
GET /docs/{slug}.md      -> one doc as Markdown (see Docs as Markdown)
GET /docs/assets/{name}  -> an image the docs show
GET /api/docs            -> JSON index of the docs
GET /robots.txt          -> disallows everything
GET /.well-known/acnologia -> this server's identity {id, name, version, public_key, url}, for sharing between servers
```

When the instance sets an access password (ACNOLOGIA_ACCESS_PASSWORD), only /healthz, /robots.txt, /.well-known/acnologia and the server to server routes under /api/peer/v1 stay public: the llms files, the docs and /api/docs answer 401 {"error":{"code":"locked"}} unless the request sends `X-Acnologia-Access: <password>` or carries the browser's gate cookie. The app token routes (/proxy, /api/v1, /mcp) are not affected.

## GET /api/v1/services

Lists the services the token may use.

```http
GET /api/v1/services
Authorization: Bearer acn_xxx
```

```json
{
  "services": [
    {
      "slug": "serpapi",
      "name": "SerpAPI",
      "provider": "serpapi",
      "category": "search",
      "available": true,
      "base_url": "https://serpapi.com",
      "auth": {"type": "query", "name": "api_key"}
    },
    {
      "slug": "elevenlabs",
      "name": "ElevenLabs",
      "provider": "elevenlabs",
      "category": "voice",
      "available": false,
      "base_url": "https://api.elevenlabs.io",
      "auth": {"type": "header", "name": "xi-api-key"}
    }
  ]
}
```

`available: false` means no key can be handed out right now (all cooling down, exhausted, invalid, or busy at their concurrency limit).

`auth.type` says where the provider expects the key:

| type | placement |
|---|---|
| `query` | query parameter `auth.name`, for example `?api_key=SECRET` |
| `header` | header `auth.name`, for example `xi-api-key: SECRET` |
| `bearer` | header `auth.name` (normally `Authorization`) set to `Bearer SECRET` |

## POST /api/v1/lease

Borrow a key. Only for apps in mode `lease` or `both`.

```http
POST /api/v1/lease
Authorization: Bearer acn_xxx
Content-Type: application/json

{"service": "serpapi", "exclude_key_ids": [12], "ttl_sec": 300, "wait_sec": 10, "exclusive": false}
```

`exclude_key_ids` (optional) skips keys you already tried. `exclusive` (optional) keeps the key from every other caller until you report or the lease expires. `ttl_sec` (optional) is how long the lease stays open; when omitted the server uses 120 seconds on services with a concurrency limit and 300 seconds otherwise. `wait_sec` (optional, 0 to 60, default 0) is how long the server may wait for a free slot when every usable key is at its concurrency limit; keep your HTTP client timeout longer than this. See [Concurrency limits](#concurrency-limits).

200:

```json
{
  "lease_id": "lse_7f3a9c",
  "key_id": 14,
  "service": "serpapi",
  "secret": "4b1e...a9F2",
  "auth": {"type": "query", "name": "api_key"},
  "base_url": "https://serpapi.com",
  "expires_at": "2026-11-01T12:05:00Z"
}
```

`auth.type` is `query` (parameter `auth.name`), `header` (header `auth.name`) or `bearer` (header `auth.name`, default `Authorization`, value `Bearer <secret>`). When `auth.prefix` is present, send `prefix + secret` instead (for example `Token <secret>`).

503 when nothing is available:

```json
{"error": {"code": "no_key_available", "message": "all keys for serpapi are cooling down"}, "retry_after_sec": 37}
```

503 when usable keys exist but every one is at its concurrency limit (and `wait_sec`, if any, ran out):

```json
{"error": {"code": "all_keys_busy", "message": "every usable key is at its concurrency limit, retry shortly"}, "retry_after_sec": 1}
```

For `no_key_available`, `retry_after_sec` is the time until the earliest cooldown ends, when known. For `all_keys_busy` it is usually 1: a slot frees as soon as another caller reports. When the keys are held back by a rate limit the provider publishes in its offers, it is the time until the first key's window frees, and the message says so. Both also set a `Retry-After` header. Selection prefers `primary` keys and only uses `backup` keys when no primary key is free; within a tier the service strategy (`round_robin`, `fill_first`, `least_used`, `most_quota`, `random`) decides.

## POST /api/v1/leases/{lease_id}/report

Tell Acnologia how the key did. Always report, including on success. On a service with a concurrency limit, reporting is also what releases the lease's slot on the key; an unreported lease blocks that slot until it expires.

```http
POST /api/v1/leases/lse_7f3a9c/report
Authorization: Bearer acn_xxx
Content-Type: application/json

{"outcome": "rate_limited", "status_code": 429, "retry_after_sec": 60, "message": "hourly limit", "rotate": true}
```

Only `outcome` is required.

```json
{"ok": true, "next": {"lease_id": "lse_81bd02", "key_id": 15, "service": "serpapi", "secret": "...", "auth": {"type": "query", "name": "api_key"}, "base_url": "https://serpapi.com", "expires_at": "2026-11-01T12:06:00Z"}}
```

With `rotate: true` the response carries a new lease on a different key in `next`, or `null` when none is available. With `rotate: false`, `next` is `null`.

Rules: report within 10 minutes after `expires_at` (later reports get 410), only once per lease (a second report gets 409), and only while the app may still use the service (403 otherwise). `retry_after_sec` is capped at 86400. Do not put the secret in `message`; Acnologia removes it anyway because messages are shown on the dashboard.

## POST /api/v1/leases/{lease_id}/renew

Extend a lease you hold, for long jobs.

```http
POST /api/v1/leases/lse_7f3a9c/renew
Authorization: Bearer acn_xxx
Content-Type: application/json

{"ttl_sec": 600}
```

200 `{"ok": true, "expires_at": "..."}`. 404 `lease_not_found` when the lease is not yours or no longer open.

### Outcomes

| outcome | when to send it | effect on the key |
|---|---|---|
| `ok` | provider call succeeded | resets consecutive failures |
| `rate_limited` | provider returned a rate limit (usually 429) | cooldown for `retry_after_sec`, else `cooldown_sec * 2^(fails-1)` capped at 1h |
| `busy` | the account is at its concurrency cap | steps aside for `retry_after_sec` (default 1s), no backoff |
| `quota_exhausted` | monthly or daily quota used up | status `exhausted` until quota reset (or 24h), then reactivated automatically |
| `invalid` | key rejected (revoked, wrong) | status `invalid`, out of rotation until a health check passes |
| `banned` | the provider suspended the account | status `banned`; only an admin reset brings it back |
| `error` | provider outage, network error, bad request | not penalized; counts toward the circuit breaker |

### Provider error mapping

| provider | response | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| SerpAPI | 429 with "run out of searches" | `quota_exhausted` |
| SerpAPI | 429 with "past hour" or "hourly" | `rate_limited` until the start of the next hour |
| SerpAPI | 401 or "Invalid API key" | `invalid` |
| ElevenLabs | 429 `too_many_concurrent_requests` | `busy` (retry 1s) |
| ElevenLabs | 429 `system_busy` | `error` |
| ElevenLabs | `detected_unusual_activity`, `account_suspended` | `banned` |
| ElevenLabs | 401 `quota_exceeded` | `quota_exhausted` |
| ElevenLabs | 401 `invalid_api_key` | `invalid` |
| OpenAI | 429 `insufficient_quota`, `credit_balance_exhausted` or a spend limit code | `quota_exhausted` |
| OpenAI, Anthropic, Groq, Mistral, Together, Fireworks, OpenRouter, Perplexity, xAI, Cohere | other 429 (honors `Retry-After`) | `rate_limited` |
| Anthropic | 429 `enforced_spend_limit_reached`, 402 `billing_error`, 400 "credit balance is too low" | `quota_exhausted` |
| Anthropic | 529 `overloaded_error` | `error` |
| xAI | 400 "Incorrect API key provided" | `invalid` |
| DeepSeek | 402 Insufficient Balance / 429 (account concurrency) / 503 | `quota_exhausted` / `busy` (retry 2s) / `error` |
| Groq | 429 naming a daily limit (RPD, TPD) / 400 `blocked_api_access` | `quota_exhausted` |
| Cohere | 429 trial key monthly cap / 498 deny listed key | `quota_exhausted` / `banned` |
| OpenRouter | 402 in flight credit hold / 402 / 403 key or budget limit / 403 moderation | `busy` / `quota_exhausted` / `quota_exhausted` / `ok` |
| Perplexity | 429 with `error.type` `overloaded` | `error` |
| generic | 429 (honors `Retry-After`) / 402 / 401 or 403 | `rate_limited` / `quota_exhausted` / `invalid` |

The proxy applies this mapping itself.

## ANY /proxy/{service}/{path}

Call Acnologia instead of the provider. Acnologia forwards to `base_url/{path}` with the same method, query string, headers and body, injects a key where `auth.type` says, and on a rate limit retries with the next key (up to the service `max_attempts`). Only for apps in mode `proxy` or `both`.

Response: the provider's status, headers and body, plus:

```
X-Acnologia-Key-Id: 14        which key served the request
X-Acnologia-Attempts: 2       how many keys were tried
X-Acnologia-Service: serpapi  which service answered (useful with groups)
X-Acnologia-Cache: hit        hit, miss or bypass, on services with caching
```

Allowed methods: GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS (others get 405). A path containing a literal `?` or `#`, or a `.` or `..` segment, gets 400 `bad_path`; percent encoded characters such as `%2F` are forwarded as sent. Provider redirects are returned to you rather than followed, with the key removed from response headers. Responses carry `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox`, so they cannot run script on the Acnologia origin.

If no key is available the proxy answers 503 `no_key_available` with `retry_after_sec`, like the lease endpoint. On a service with a concurrency limit, a request that finds every key busy waits in a queue for up to the service `queue_timeout_sec` (ElevenLabs default 30s); if no slot frees up in time the proxy answers 503 `all_keys_busy`. The proxy never sends more than a key's limit in parallel, so you do not need your own throttling. It also keeps each key under the rate limits its provider publishes in `offers` (for example TinyFish Search: 30 requests a minute and 500 an hour per key): a key at a limit is skipped, then the request waits up to `queue_timeout_sec`, then it gets 503 `all_keys_busy` with `retry_after_sec`.

### SerpAPI

```bash
curl -s "http://localhost:8080/proxy/serpapi/search.json?engine=google&q=best+espresso+grinder" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer acn_xxx"
```

Equivalent to `https://serpapi.com/search.json?engine=google&q=...&api_key=SECRET`. For URL-only tools:

```
http://localhost:8080/proxy/serpapi/search.json?engine=google&q=coffee&acn_token=acn_xxx
```

### ElevenLabs

```bash
curl -s -X POST "http://localhost:8080/proxy/elevenlabs/v1/text-to-speech/21m00Tcm4TlvDq8ikWAM" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer acn_xxx" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Accept: audio/mpeg" \
  -d '{"text": "Hello from Acnologia.", "model_id": "eleven_multilingual_v2"}' \
  -o hello.mp3
```

Equivalent to calling `https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/text-to-speech/{voice_id}` with `xi-api-key: SECRET`.

### LLM providers

OpenAI, Together AI, Groq, Mistral, Fireworks AI, DeepSeek, xAI, Cerebras, OpenRouter and Perplexity take a bearer key, so an OpenAI compatible client works with the proxy as its base URL (`http://localhost:8080/proxy/groq/v1` for Groq, `.../proxy/openai/v1` for OpenAI) and the Acnologia token as its API key:

```bash
curl -s -X POST "http://localhost:8080/proxy/groq/v1/chat/completions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer acn_xxx" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "openai/gpt-oss-20b", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello"}]}'
```

Anthropic takes the key in `x-api-key`. Send `anthropic-version` yourself (the Anthropic SDKs do); the proxy forwards it:

```bash
curl -s -X POST "http://localhost:8080/proxy/anthropic/v1/messages" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer acn_xxx" \
  -H "anthropic-version: 2023-06-01" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "claude-haiku-5-5", "max_tokens": 64, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello"}]}'
```

## Concurrency limits

Some providers cap simultaneous requests per key (ElevenLabs returns 429 `too_many_concurrent_requests`). Acnologia enforces a per key limit so that never happens:

- Each service has `max_concurrency` (0 means unlimited); a key can override it. ElevenLabs defaults to 2 per key.
- Each service has `queue_timeout_sec`, how long proxied requests wait for a slot. ElevenLabs defaults to 30s.
- A lease on a limited service is exclusive: it holds one slot on its key from issue until it is reported or `expires_at` passes. Default TTL is 120s on limited services (300s otherwise), so pass a `ttl_sec` close to how long you need the key.
- Lease callers choose between failing fast (`wait_sec` omitted or 0, 503 `all_keys_busy` at once) and waiting (`wait_sec` up to 60).
- `all_keys_busy` is not a key problem: do not report anything for it and do not exclude keys. Retry after `retry_after_sec` or lease again with `wait_sec`.

Report every lease, on every path (success, provider error, exception, timeout). The SDK `with_key` helpers do this for you; with a manual lease, report in a `finally` block.

## Lease mode flow

1. `POST /api/v1/lease {"service": "serpapi"}` (add `"wait_sec": n` to wait for a busy key instead of getting 503 `all_keys_busy`).
2. Call `base_url` yourself with `secret` placed per `auth`.
3. On success: report `{"outcome": "ok"}`.
4. On rate limit / quota / invalid key: report that outcome with `"rotate": true`, then retry with `next`. If `next` is null, lease again with `exclude_key_ids` set to the keys already tried; a 503 means wait `retry_after_sec`.
5. On any other failure: report `{"outcome": "error", "message": "..."}`.
6. Never skip the report: on limited services the lease holds a concurrency slot until reported or expired.

Never log or persist `secret`.

## MCP

`POST /mcp` is a Model Context Protocol endpoint (streamable HTTP transport, JSON responses, no SSE needed). Authenticate with the same app token header. Use `initialize`, then `tools/list` for the authoritative input schemas, then `tools/call`.

```sh
# Claude Code, over HTTP
claude mcp add --transport http acnologia http://localhost:8080/mcp \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer acn_xxx"

# Clients that only speak stdio, such as Claude Desktop
acnologia mcp --url http://localhost:8080 --token acn_xxx
```

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "acnologia": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "http://localhost:8080/mcp",
      "headers": {"Authorization": "Bearer acn_xxx"}
    }
  }
}
```

Each app chooses its tool sets on the dashboard Apps page. Core, service tools, resources and prompts are on by default; insights and manage are off.

| set | tool | purpose | typical arguments |
|---|---|---|---|
| core | `list_services` | services the token may use, with availability | none |
| core | `pool_status` | whether a service has a key available now | `service` |
| core | `get_key` | lease a key (lease mode apps only); always follow with `report_key` | `service`, optional `exclusive`, `exclude_key_ids`, `ttl_sec` (max 86400), `wait_sec` (0 to 60) |
| core | `renew_key` | extend a lease for a long job | `lease_id`, optional `ttl_sec` |
| core | `report_key` | report a lease outcome, optionally rotate | `lease_id`, `outcome` (`ok`, `rate_limited`, `busy`, `quota_exhausted`, `invalid`, `banned`, `error`), optional `retry_after_sec`, `message`, `rotate` |
| core | `proxy_request` | make a provider call through the proxy without seeing a key | `service`, `path`, optional `method`, `query`, `body` |
| service tools | one per provider example, named after the service and the example | ready to call endpoints, such as a SerpAPI search; the description names the matching offer, whether it is free and its per key limits | the example's path and query parameters, `extra_query`, `body` |
| insights | `list_keys`, `key_details`, `service_stats` | read only key health, quota and recent events, never a secret | `service`, `validity`, `key_id` |
| manage | `check_keys`, `set_key_status`, `add_keys` | run health checks, enable or disable a key, add keys | `service`, `key_id`, `status`, `keys` |

Resources: `acnologia://services`, `acnologia://services/{slug}` and `acnologia://llms.txt`. Prompts: `use_service` and `key_health_report`. Per app settings also cap tool results (`max_result_kb`, default 200), make `get_key` exclusive by default, add instructions and hide single tools.

Example call:

```json
{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 3, "method": "tools/call",
 "params": {"name": "proxy_request",
            "arguments": {"service": "serpapi", "method": "GET", "path": "/search.json",
                          "query": {"engine": "google", "q": "coffee"}}}}
```

Prefer `proxy_request` or a service tool over `get_key` so secrets never enter the model context. `proxy_request` also queues for busy keys like the proxy does. If you do use `get_key`, call `report_key` for every lease: on concurrency limited services an unreported lease keeps the key's slot busy until `ttl_sec` runs out.

## SDKs

There are SDKs for Python, TypeScript, Go, PHP, Ruby, Rust, Java, Kotlin, C#, Swift, Dart and C++. None is on a package registry yet; [the SDK index](/docs/sdks.md) shows how to install each one today and how to run its tests.

All SDKs share the same shape: `services`, `lease` (returns a lease with `report`, `renew` and `apply`), `with_key` or `withKey` (calls your function, reports, and rotates when you raise a rate limit, quota or invalid key error), and `proxy(service)` returning raw responses. On the last allowed attempt `with_key` reports without rotating and re-raises. Every client also reads `ACNOLOGIA_URL` and `ACNOLOGIA_TOKEN`, and never prints a secret or token.

Every SDK also takes an `exclusive` lease option (sent as `exclusive: true`; `with_key` passes it to the leases it takes itself), renews an open lease (`POST /api/v1/leases/{id}/renew`, which updates the lease's expiry; 404 `lease_not_found` is the generic API error), and raises a dedicated error for 503 `service_unavailable` (the circuit breaker is open) that carries the retry after and is not a no key error.

Concurrency support is the same everywhere: `lease` and `with_key` take a wait option that is sent as `wait_sec`, a 503 `all_keys_busy` raises a busy error that is a subtype of (or, in Go, the same type as) the no key error so existing handlers keep working, and `with_key` reports every lease it takes, whatever the callback does, so slots are released at once.

| SDK | wait option | busy error |
|---|---|---|
| Python | `lease(..., wait_sec=20)`, `with_key(..., wait_sec=20)` | `AllKeysBusy` (subclass of `NoKeyAvailable`), `.busy` |
| TypeScript | `lease(s, { waitSec: 20 })`, `withKey(s, fn, { waitSec: 20 })` | `AllKeysBusyError` (extends `NoKeyAvailableError`), `.busy` |
| Go | `LeaseOptions{Wait: 20 * time.Second}`, `WithWait(20 * time.Second)` | `*ErrNoKeyAvailable` with `Busy: true`, matches `acnologia.AllKeysBusy` |
| PHP | `lease($s, waitSec: 20)`, `withKey($s, $fn, waitSec: 20)` | `Acnologia\Exception\AllKeysBusy` (extends `NoKeyAvailable`), `->busy` |
| Ruby | `lease(s, wait_sec: 20)`, `with_key(s, wait_sec: 20)` | `Acnologia::AllKeysBusy` (subclass of `NoKeyAvailable`), `busy?` |
| Rust | `LeaseOptions::new().wait(..)`, `WithKeyOptions::new().wait(..)` | `Error::AllKeysBusy`, `is_no_key_available()` covers both |
| Java | `LeaseOptions.builder().waitFor(..)`, `WithKeyOptions.builder().waitFor(..)` | `AllKeysBusyException` (extends `NoKeyAvailableException`) |
| Kotlin | `LeaseOptions(wait = 20.seconds)` | `AllKeysBusyException` (extends `NoKeyAvailableException`) |
| C# | `new LeaseOptions { Wait = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(20) }` | `AllKeysBusyException` (extends `NoKeyAvailableException`) |
| Swift | `LeaseOptions(wait: 20)` | `AcnologiaError.allKeysBusy`, `isNoKeyAvailable` covers both |
| Dart | `lease(s, wait: Duration(seconds: 20))`, `withKey(s, fn, wait: ..)` | `AllKeysBusyException` (extends `NoKeyAvailableException`) |
| C++ | `LeaseOptions::wait` | `AllKeysBusy` (derives from `NoKeyAvailable`) |

| SDK | renew | exclusive | circuit breaker open |
|---|---|---|---|
| Python | `lease.renew(ttl_sec=600)` | `lease(s, exclusive=True)` | `ServiceUnavailable` |
| TypeScript | `await lease.renew(600)` | `lease(s, { exclusive: true })` | `ServiceUnavailableError` |
| Go | `l.Renew(ctx, 10*time.Minute)` | `LeaseOptions{Exclusive: true}` | `*ErrServiceUnavailable`, matches `acnologia.ServiceUnavailable` |
| PHP | `$lease->renew(600)` | `lease($s, exclusive: true)` | `Acnologia\Exception\ServiceUnavailable` |
| Ruby | `lease.renew(ttl_sec: 600)` | `lease(s, exclusive: true)` | `Acnologia::ServiceUnavailable` |
| Rust | `lease.renew(Some(Duration::from_secs(600)))` | `LeaseOptions::new().exclusive(true)` | `Error::ServiceUnavailable` |
| Java | `lease.renew(Duration.ofMinutes(10))` | `LeaseOptions.builder().exclusive(true)` | `ServiceUnavailableException` |
| Kotlin | `lease.renew(10.minutes)` | `LeaseOptions(exclusive = true)` | `ServiceUnavailableException` |
| C# | `await lease.RenewAsync(TimeSpan.FromMinutes(10))` | `new LeaseOptions { Exclusive = true }` | `ServiceUnavailableException` |
| Swift | `try await lease.renew(ttl: 600)` | `LeaseOptions(exclusive: true)` | `AcnologiaError.serviceUnavailable` |
| Dart | `await lease.renew(ttl: Duration(minutes: 10))` | `lease(s, exclusive: true)` | `ServiceUnavailableException` |
| C++ | `lease.renew(std::chrono::minutes(10))` | `LeaseOptions::exclusive` | `acnologia::ServiceUnavailable` |

### Python

```bash
pip install acnologia
```

```python
import httpx
from acnologia import Acnologia, RateLimited

acn = Acnologia("http://localhost:8080", "acn_xxx")

r = acn.proxy("serpapi").get("/search.json", params={"engine": "google", "q": "coffee"})

def search(lease):
    resp = httpx.get(lease.url("/search.json"), params=lease.apply({"q": "coffee"}))
    if resp.status_code == 429:
        raise RateLimited(retry_after=3600)
    return resp.json()

data = acn.with_key("serpapi", search)
```

Also `AsyncAcnologia`. Exceptions: `AcnologiaError`, `NoKeyAvailable`, `AllKeysBusy`, `RateLimited`, `QuotaExhausted`, `InvalidKey`.

### TypeScript and JavaScript

```bash
npm install @acnologia/keys
```

```ts
import { Acnologia, RateLimitedError } from "@acnologia/keys"; // or: const { Acnologia } = require("@acnologia/keys")

const acn = new Acnologia({ baseUrl: "http://localhost:8080", token: "acn_xxx" });

const res = await acn.proxy("elevenlabs").post("/v1/text-to-speech/21m00Tcm4TlvDq8ikWAM", {
  text: "Hello", model_id: "eleven_multilingual_v2",
});

const data = await acn.withKey("serpapi", async (lease) => {
  const { query } = lease.apply({ query: { engine: "google", q: "coffee" } });
  const r = await fetch(`${lease.baseUrl}/search.json?${new URLSearchParams(query as Record<string, string>)}`);
  if (r.status === 429) throw new RateLimitedError(3600);
  return r.json();
});
```

Errors: `AcnologiaError`, `NoKeyAvailableError`, `AllKeysBusyError`, `RateLimitedError`, `QuotaExhaustedError`, `InvalidKeyError`.

### Go

```bash
go get github.com/sidharthpunathil/acnologia/sdk/go
```

```go
c := acnologia.New("http://localhost:8080", "acn_xxx")
resp, err := c.Proxy("serpapi").Get(ctx, "/search.json", url.Values{"q": {"coffee"}})

err = c.WithKey(ctx, "serpapi", func(l *acnologia.Lease) error {
	req, _ := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, "GET", l.URL("/search.json", url.Values{"q": {"coffee"}}), nil)
	l.Apply(req)
	res, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer res.Body.Close()
	if res.StatusCode == 429 {
		return &acnologia.ErrRateLimited{RetryAfter: time.Hour}
	}
	return nil
})
```

Errors match sentinels with `errors.Is`: `acnologia.RateLimited`, `acnologia.QuotaExhausted`, `acnologia.InvalidKey`, `acnologia.NoKeyAvailable`, `acnologia.AllKeysBusy`.

### Rust


```rust
use acnologia::{check_status, Client};

let acn = Client::new("http://localhost:8080", "acn_xxx")?; // or Client::from_env()
let resp = acn.proxy("serpapi").get("/search.json", &[("q", "coffee")]).await?;

let http = reqwest::Client::new();
let body = acn
    .with_key("serpapi", |lease| {
        let http = http.clone();
        async move {
            let req = http.get(lease.url("/search.json", &[("q", "coffee")]));
            let resp = check_status(lease.apply(req).send().await?)?; // 429, 402, 401, 403 rotate
            Ok(resp.text().await?)
        }
    })
    .await?;
```

Errors: `acnologia::Error` with `NoKeyAvailable`, `AllKeysBusy`, `ServiceUnavailable`, `Unauthenticated`, `Forbidden`, `Api`, `RateLimited`, `QuotaExhausted`, `InvalidKey`. A `blocking` feature adds a synchronous client.

### Java

```sh
cd sdk/java && mvn install   # dev.acnologia:acnologia:0.1.0, Java 17+
```

```java
Acnologia acn = Acnologia.create("http://localhost:8080", "acn_xxx"); // or Acnologia.fromEnv()
HttpResponse<byte[]> res = acn.proxy("serpapi").get("/search.json", Map.of("q", "coffee"));

HttpClient http = HttpClient.newHttpClient();
String json = acn.withKey("serpapi", lease -> {
    HttpRequest req = lease.apply(HttpRequest.newBuilder(URI.create(lease.url("/search.json", Map.of("q", "coffee")))).build());
    HttpResponse<String> r = http.send(req, HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.ofString());
    if (r.statusCode() == 429) throw new RateLimitedException(Duration.ofHours(1), 429, null);
    return r.body();
});
```

Exceptions: `NoKeyAvailableException`, `AllKeysBusyException`, `ServiceUnavailableException`, `RateLimitedException`, `QuotaExhaustedException`, `InvalidKeyException`.

### C#

```sh
dotnet add YourApp.csproj reference path/to/acnologia/sdk/csharp/src/Acnologia/Acnologia.csproj   # .NET 8
```

```csharp
using var acn = new AcnologiaClient("http://localhost:8080", "acn_xxx"); // or AcnologiaClient.FromEnvironment()
using var resp = await acn.Proxy("serpapi").GetAsync("/search.json", new Dictionary<string, string> { ["q"] = "coffee" });

var http = new HttpClient();
var json = await acn.WithKeyAsync("serpapi", async (lease, ct) =>
{
    using var req = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Get, lease.Url("/search.json", new Dictionary<string, string> { ["q"] = "coffee" }));
    lease.Apply(req);
    using var r = await http.SendAsync(req, ct);
    if ((int)r.StatusCode == 429) throw new RateLimitedException(TimeSpan.FromHours(1), 429);
    return await r.Content.ReadAsStringAsync(ct);
});
```

Exceptions: `NoKeyAvailableException`, `AllKeysBusyException`, `ServiceUnavailableException`, `UnauthenticatedException`, `ForbiddenException`, `AcnologiaApiException`, and the rotation exceptions `RateLimitedException`, `QuotaExhaustedException`, `InvalidKeyException`.

### Swift

```swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/sidharthpunathil/acnologia", branch: "main") // product "Acnologia", package "acnologia"
```

```swift
import Acnologia

let acn = try Acnologia(baseURL: "http://localhost:8080", token: "acn_xxx") // or Acnologia.fromEnvironment()
let resp = try await acn.proxy("serpapi").get("/search.json", query: [URLQueryItem(name: "q", value: "coffee")])

let data: Data = try await acn.withKey("serpapi") { lease in
    var req = URLRequest(url: try lease.url("/search.json", query: [URLQueryItem(name: "q", value: "coffee")]))
    lease.apply(to: &req)
    let (data, r) = try await URLSession.shared.data(for: req)
    if (r as? HTTPURLResponse)?.statusCode == 429 { throw AcnologiaError.rateLimited(retryAfter: 3600, statusCode: 429) }
    return data
}
```

Errors are cases of `AcnologiaError`: `.noKeyAvailable`, `.allKeysBusy`, `.serviceUnavailable`, `.unauthenticated`, `.forbidden`, `.api`, and the rotation cases `.rateLimited`, `.quotaExhausted`, `.invalidKey`.


```dart
  final resp = await http.Response.fromStream(
      await client.send(lease.request('GET', '/search.json', query: {'q': 'coffee'})));
```

```cpp
#include <acnologia/acnologia.hpp>

acnologia::Client client("http://localhost:8080", "acn_xxx"); // or acnologia::Client::from_env()
auto resp = client.proxy("serpapi").get("/search.json", {{"q", "coffee"}});

std::string body = client.with_key("serpapi", [](acnologia::Lease& lease) {
    std::string url = lease.signed_url("/search.json", {{"q", "coffee"}}); // query auth; lease.apply() for headers
    auto [status, text] = my_http_get(url);                               // any HTTP library
    if (status == 429) throw acnologia::RateLimited(std::chrono::hours(1), 429);
    return text;
});
```

Exceptions derive from `acnologia::ApiError`: `NoKeyAvailable`, `AllKeysBusy`, `ServiceUnavailable`, plus the rotation exceptions `RateLimited`, `QuotaExhausted`, `InvalidKey`.

### Other languages

Each service's Integrate tab in the dashboard has copy ready snippets for curl and every SDK above, filled in with the service's slug, base URL and auth placement. For any other language, use the HTTP client your project already has: proxy mode is one call; lease mode leases, calls the provider with the key where the service expects it, and reports the outcome.

## Resilience

### Circuit breaker

Every service has a circuit breaker. Provider errors (5xx, timeouts, refused connections) count toward it; rate limits, bad keys and client errors do not. After `breaker_threshold` errors within `breaker_window_sec` (defaults: 10 in 60s) the breaker opens and the proxy answers at once:

```http
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
Retry-After: 30

{"error": {"code": "service_unavailable", "message": "SerpAPI keeps failing, so Acnologia paused traffic to it"}, "retry_after_sec": 30}
```

After `breaker_reset_sec` (default 30s) one probe request goes through. Success closes the breaker; another provider error opens it again. Keys are never penalized for a provider outage. Set `breaker_threshold` to `-1` in a provider spec to turn it off.

### Busy and banned keys

- `busy` (for example ElevenLabs `too_many_concurrent_requests`): the key is healthy but at its concurrency cap. Acnologia rotates to the next key immediately and parks this one for about a second, without raising its failure count.
- `banned` (for example ElevenLabs `detected_unusual_activity`): the provider suspended the account. The key leaves rotation with status `banned`. Health checks skip it; an operator reset (`POST /api/admin/keys/{id}/reset`) brings it back.

### Quota from response headers

Providers that report quota on every response (Brave Search sends `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 1, 1999`) declare it in the spec:

```json
"quota": {"unit": "queries", "headers": {"limit": "X-RateLimit-Limit", "remaining": "X-RateLimit-Remaining", "reset": "X-RateLimit-Reset", "reset_format": "seconds", "index": 1}}
```

Each proxied response then updates the key's quota. When the provider reports 0 left, the key is parked until the reset it announced.

## Response cache and idempotency

A service with `cache_ttl_sec` above 0 (search providers default to 3600) caches successful GET responses up to 1 MB in memory, keyed by path, sorted query and `Accept`. Hits cost no quota and add `X-Acnologia-Cache: hit`. Misses say `miss`; uncacheable responses say `bypass`. Acnologia never caches responses made with hidden or restricted keys, responses marked `no-store` or `private`, or bodies that contain the key. Send `Cache-Control: no-cache` to skip the cache for one request. `ACNOLOGIA_CACHE_MB` sets the memory cap (default 64, 0 turns caching off).

`Idempotency-Key` works on any method. The first response (below 500) is stored per app for 10 minutes and replayed with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`, so a retried POST does not spend twice.

## Service groups

A group puts several services behind one slug, for example two SerpAPI accounts owned by different teams, or one API in two regions:

```http
GET /proxy/search/search.json?q=coffee
Authorization: Bearer acn_...
```

Acnologia tries the first member. It moves to the next when the member has no usable key, its breaker is open, it cannot be reached, or every key it tried was rate limited, busy, exhausted, invalid or banned. A request the provider rejects as malformed (400, 422) is relayed as is, since it would fail everywhere. `X-Acnologia-Service` names the member that answered. An app allowed to use the group may use its members through it.

## App limits and spend

Each app can have `daily_requests`, `monthly_requests`, `daily_budget` and `monthly_budget` (USD, UTC days and months). Cost per request comes from a service override, else the price of the provider offer that matches the request (free offers cost 0), else the provider spec's `quota.cost_per_request`. Cache hits are free and do not count as requests. A lease counts as one request when it is issued. Over a limit, proxy and lease calls answer:

```http
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 4210

{"error": {"code": "app_limit_reached", "message": "this app reached its daily requests limit"}, "limit": "daily_requests", "reset_at": "2026-11-02T00:00:00Z", "retry_after_sec": 4210}
```

## Egress proxies

Operators can route a service's or a single key's traffic through an HTTP, HTTPS or SOCKS5 proxy (`socks5h://` resolves DNS at the proxy). A key's proxy wins over its service's. Proxy URLs are encrypted at rest and shown without credentials. Health checks use the same route.

## Webhooks

Webhooks receive pool events: `key.invalid`, `key.banned`, `key.exhausted`, `key.recovered`, `quota.low` (under 10% left), `pool.empty`, `service.down`, `service.up`, `app.limit`. Formats: `json`, `slack`, `discord`, `telegram` (use `https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/sendMessage?chat_id=<id>`). Repeats of the same event about the same key, service or app are sent at most once per 10 minutes. Hidden keys never produce events. By default webhook URLs may not point at private addresses; set `ACNOLOGIA_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_PRIVATE=true` for an internal receiver.

JSON deliveries carry:

```http
X-Acnologia-Event: key.exhausted
X-Acnologia-Timestamp: 1793577600
X-Acnologia-Signature: sha256=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<timestamp>.<body>" with the signing secret>

{"type": "key.exhausted", "ts": "2026-11-01T22:00:00Z", "message": "SerpAPI key \"acct-3\" is out of quota", "service_id": 1, "service": "serpapi", "key_id": 3, "key": "acct-3"}
```

The signing secret (`whsec_...`) is shown once when the webhook is created. Reject deliveries whose timestamp is more than a few minutes old. Payloads pass the redactor, so they never carry a key.

## AI models

AI features run on a Claude model a superadmin picks under Settings, AI: a default plus optional models for `assistant`, `builder`, `fill`, `summary` (chat compaction summaries) and `refresh` (re-checking provider offers). Per call, the feature's own model wins, then the saved default, then `ACNOLOGIA_AI_MODEL`, then `claude-opus-5-5`. A switch applies on the next call with no restart; a builder run keeps the model it was queued with. `GET /api/admin/ai/models` (admin) lists the models with context window and price per million tokens, from Anthropic's Models API when a key is set or Acnologia's built in table otherwise, plus the saved and effective choice. `PUT /api/admin/ai/models` (superadmin) saves `{default, assistant, builder, fill, summary, refresh}`, each a model id or `""`. Cost on the Usage page is priced at the model that answered.

## Key secrecy and redaction

- Proxy mode and MCP `proxy_request` never show a key to the caller. Response headers are scrubbed of the key, and redirects are returned, not followed.
- Leasing (`/api/v1/lease`, MCP `get_key`) returns the secret by design. Use proxy mode for any client you would not hand a key to.
- Every request Acnologia sends to Claude (the Assistant, the provider builder, Fill with AI, run naming) passes a redactor first. Known secrets (every pool key, webhook URLs and secrets, egress proxy URLs, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, a builder run's test keys, keys pasted in a chat) become `[key ...c21e]`. Unknown secrets found by pattern (prefixes such as `sk-`, `AIza`, `ghp_`, `tvly-`, `AKIA`, `acn_`, JWTs, `Bearer` and `Basic` values, `key=` and `token=` fields, long random tokens) become `[secret ...c21e]`.
- Keys pasted into the Assistant go to an encrypted per thread vault; the model sees placeholders such as `[key k3 ...c21e]` and tools resolve them on the server. The stored user message keeps only the prose and a list of label plus last four characters.
- Long Assistant chats are compacted: past 60% of the Assistant model's context window (or `ACNOLOGIA_CHAT_COMPACT_TOKENS`), Claude summarizes the older messages from the already redacted history, the summary is redacted again, and it replaces them in what the model is sent. The last 6 messages stay verbatim and the transcript keeps everything. `POST /api/admin/chat/threads/{id}/compact` compacts on request.
- The same scrub runs on events, the audit log, key `last_error`, agent steps and run errors, webhook payloads and every log line.
- Limit: a short key with no prefix and no `key=` in front of it is caught only if it is already a pool key or the paste parser finds it.

## Errors

| Status | Code | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | `bad_path` | Proxy path with a literal `?`, `#`, or a `.` / `..` segment. |
| 401 | `unauthenticated` | Token missing or wrong. |
| 403 | `unauthenticated`, `service_not_allowed`, `proxy_not_allowed`, `lease_not_allowed` | App disabled, or not allowed this service or mode. |
| 404 | `lease_not_found` | Renewing a lease that is not open. |
| 405 | `method_not_allowed` | Proxy method other than GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS. |
| 409 | `report_failed` | Lease already reported. |
| 410 | `report_failed` | Lease expired more than 10 minutes ago. |
| 413 | `body_too_large` | Proxy body over `ACNOLOGIA_MAX_BODY_MB` (default 50). |
| 429 | `app_limit_reached` | The app used up a daily or monthly request or budget limit; `limit` and `reset_at` say which and until when. |
| 502 | `upstream_unreachable` | The provider could not be reached on the first attempt. |
| 503 | `no_key_available` | Every usable key is cooling down, exhausted or disabled. Wait `retry_after_sec`. |
| 503 | `all_keys_busy` | Usable keys exist but all are at their concurrency limit or at a rate limit their provider publishes. Retry after `retry_after_sec` or lease with `wait_sec`. |
| 503 | `service_unavailable` | The provider keeps failing and its circuit breaker is open. Wait `retry_after_sec`. |
| 503 | `empty_group` | The group has no services left. |
| 403 | `share_revoked`, `share_paused`, `share_expired` | A service another Acnologia shares with this one was revoked, paused or expired by its owner. Also sent as `X-Acnologia-Share`. Revoked is final; paused may come back. |
| 403 | `lease_not_allowed` | Leasing a service another Acnologia shares with this one. Use the proxy. |
| 508 | `loop_detected` | The request passed through more than 3 Acnologia servers. |

## Services shared by another Acnologia

A service in `GET /api/v1/services` whose provider is `acnologia-peer` is shared by another Acnologia server: this server forwards your proxied call to that server, which injects one of its own keys. Use it through `/proxy/{service}/{path}` like any other service. It cannot be leased, because a lease would hand out the share token. Errors the other server relays from the provider reach you unchanged; when the owner pauses or revokes the share you get 403 `share_paused` or `share_revoked`. The owner may limit a shared service to some of its keys, so the other server can run out of keys (503 `no_key_available`) while the owner's own apps still have some; the manifest's `available` count reflects only the keys shared with you.

## Admin API tokens and the acn CLI

Install the `acn` client (macOS and Linux; it checks the release's SHA256SUMS and installs to /usr/local/bin when writable, else ~/.local/bin), or use `go install`:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sidharthpunathil/acnologia/main/install.sh | sh
go install github.com/sidharthpunathil/acnologia/server/cmd/acn@latest
```

Sign in through the browser with `acn login` (or `acn login --domain https://keys.example.com --no-browser`). It asks for the server URL (a bare host means https; http only for localhost), shows a one-time code like `WDJB-MJHT` and opens `/cli/authorize?code=WDJB-MJHT`. After you unlock the site, sign in and approve with a scope, the CLI receives an admin API token named `acn on <hostname>` that lasts 90 days, and prints `Signed in to <host> as <email> (<scope>)`. A valid admin token passes the site lock, so the CLI never needs the site password.

The device flow behind it (RFC 8628 style): `POST /api/cli/device {client, hostname, os}` returns `{device_code, user_code, verification_uri, verification_uri_complete, expires_in: 600, interval: 5}`; `POST /api/cli/device/token {device_code}` answers 400 with `authorization_pending`, `slow_down` (plus a longer `interval`), `access_denied` or `expired_token`, then 200 `{token, token_id, user, scope, expires_at}` once. Both are open in the site lock. `GET /api/cli/device/lookup?user_code=`, `POST /api/cli/device/approve {user_code, scope, label}` and `POST /api/cli/device/deny {user_code}` need a dashboard session.

Create tokens in the dashboard (Account, API tokens) or with `POST /api/admin/tokens {"name": "ci", "scope": "write", "expires_in_days": 90}`. Scopes: `read` (member), `write` (admin), `admin` (superadmin), capped at the creator's role. Tokens cannot manage tokens or change the account. Send them as `Authorization: Bearer acnadm_...` to any `/api/admin/` endpoint.

```sh
acn login                                      # browser sign in
acn login https://keys.example.com --token acnadm_... --name prod
acn whoami
acn status                                     # server version and pool overview
acn keys add serpapi < keys.txt                # one per line: secret, or label,secret
acn keys check serpapi
acn events --service serpapi --kind rate_limited
acn breaker serpapi --reset
acn usage 3
acn services --json
acn logout                                     # revokes the token, then forgets the server
```

The CLI stores servers per host in `acnologia/ctl.json` under the user config folder (mode 0600, folder 0700). `ACNOLOGIA_URL` and `ACNOLOGIA_TOKEN` override it for one command, for CI. `acn contexts` lists saved servers and `acn use <host>` switches; `services`, `keys <service>` and `cache purge <service>` round out the commands, and `--json` prints raw JSON for `whoami`, `status`, `services`, `keys`, `events` and `usage`. Every command also works as `acnologia ctl <command>` from the server binary.

## Docs as Markdown

This reference covers the consumer API. The rest of the docs are served as raw Markdown (`text/markdown`, no auth) at `/docs/{slug}.md`, and rendered for people at `/docs/{slug}`. `GET /api/docs` lists them as JSON: `{"docs": [{"slug", "title", "description", "size"}]}`.

- [/docs/overview.md](/docs/overview.md): what Acnologia does, quick start and features.
- [/docs/api.md](/docs/api.md): consumer error codes and the dashboard API with required roles.
- [/docs/cli.md](/docs/cli.md): the acn command line client, browser sign in, commands and CI variables.
- [/docs/configuration.md](/docs/configuration.md): environment variables, per service settings, self-hosting, backups and upgrading.
- [/docs/architecture.md](/docs/architecture.md): components, packages, request pipeline, data model and background work.
- [/docs/flows.md](/docs/flows.md): diagrams of the proxy, key selection, leases, key states, health checks, sign in, MCP and the AI builder.
- [/docs/security.md](/docs/security.md): roles, key flags, hidden keys, what the model can see, secrets at rest, web protections and outbound requests.
- [/docs/providers.md](/docs/providers.md): built in providers, the spec format, and adding one by hand or with AI.
- [/docs/development.md](/docs/development.md): setup, layout, tests and conventions.
